newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies end lower before report.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies end lower before report.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures ended lower as evening up and long liquidation ahead of USDA's Hogs and Pigs report weighed on prices, traders said.

Hogs as well as pork bellies had been exceptionally strong going into the report and traders long the market said they were nervous about holding too large a position into the report despite expectations it will show lower-than-year-ago hog numbers.
Average indications on the quarterly report point to all hogs as of September 1 at 96.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 95 to 97.5 percent.

Kept for breeding estimates averaged 96.8 percent in a range of 94 to 99 percent and kept for market estimates averaged 96.5 and ranged 95 to 98 percent of last year. Farrowing intentions for September/November and December/February averaged near 100 percent with the high end at 105 percent.
Hog futures started higher following another round of price gains in the cash pork complex and live markets before easing to trade lower most of the day.
Pork cutout values Thursday jumped to highest levels since August 21 at $74.31 to $80.56 per cwt.
Similarly, cash hog prices which ranged from $57.00 to $59.25 per cwt Friday marked the highest level since August 27.

Pork belly futures also tumbled for a limit loss of 2.00 cents in March after midday as long liquidation touched off sell stops. Futures had posted some early gains on support generated by the strong cash belly market, but pressure developed on talk that product offerings would increase next week. Prices dipped sharply on the stops before late evening up pared losses, traders said.

Early demand reflected advances in cash belly prices, which rose to $82 per cwt Thursday, the highest level since August 28. Slicers demand has been strong recently, to meet strong bacon demand. However, hog kills are seen up and more product will be available in the near term, traders added.
Hog futures closed 0.050 to 0.800 cent a lb lower with October off 0.050 at 57.350 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.675 to 0.975 cent lower with February off most at 77.575 cents.
